data_quality_notes: July 2026 values read directly from the raw InfoSparks CSVs in data/imports/mls_stats/2026-08-17/ (Dana Point column) and cross-checked against data/market_stats/2026-07_market_moves.json. Both agree on all eight metrics.

FILTER CHANGE from the prior Dana Point file: 2026-07_dana_point_sfr.json used 'Residential, Single Family, Detached' from a Dana Point-specific pull, while this pull uses 'Residential, Single Family' across all four segments. The series are close but not identical (May 2026 median reads $3,450,000 here versus $3,150,000 in the detached-only file). Do not mix the two series in a month-over-month comparison.
No median price per square foot in this pull. That metric came from the separate 2026-07-15_dana_point export and is not part of the standard multi-city market-moves set.

Houses slowed in July, not just the city-wide all-residential figure. Median days active jumped to 38 from 13 in June and 30 a year ago, and pendings fell to 19, down 24% year over year. Months of supply loosened to 3.7 from 3.2 in June, though it is still below 4.1 a year ago.

The $2,067,500 median is down 12.9% year over year, but Dana Point closes roughly 24 single-family homes a month. At that count the median tracks transaction mix as much as value. The May-to-July walk ($3.45M, $2.10M, $2.07M) is mix, not a 40% collapse.
This corroborates the Pacific Sotheby's August 1 deck, which put Dana Point city-wide expected market time at 140 days against 123 a year ago.
market_summary: Dana Point single-family cooled in July. Homes took a median of 38 days to go active-to-pending, up from 13 in June and 30 a year ago, and new pendings fell 24% year over year to 19. Supply is still tighter than last year at 3.7 months against 4.1, so this is a demand-side slowdown rather than an inventory build. The $2.07M median is down year over year on a mix that skewed lower, at transaction counts too small to read as a price move.
